summary: When the page is on-premises Outlook Web Access with forms-based authentication, the sign-in is the one logonForm at /owa/auth/logon.aspx on the server's own origin, already reviewed in this repository for the exchange-owa profile. No steps file: the format cannot express what that login needs, so the existing adapter stays the login.

sources.title: The reviewed selectors of the exchange-owa profile
The shared Exchange forms-based authentication adapter
sources.note: Line 127 accepts the page on the lower-cased pathname /owa/auth/logon.aspx. Lines 71-119 require a same-origin POST to /owa/auth.owa and one hidden destination field under /owa. Lines 136-154 require the sign-in control to be the page's own clkLgn() handler.

sources.title: The synthetic logon form the adapter is tested against
sources.note: Lines 272-294 drive the same form on /OWA/Auth/Logon.aspx, so the path is matched without regard to letter case.

sources.title: On-premises Exchange OWA login: supported form and interactive cases

selectors.note: A div with role button, not a submit control. The adapter clicks it only while it carries the page's clkLgn() handler; a fixture may not hold an inline handler, so the fixture has the element without it.

fixtures.note: The form, its POST action /owa/auth.owa, the hidden destination field and the two fields of the test's synthetic page.

staysInteractive.note: AD FS or another federation, and Windows authentication (NTLM or Kerberos): the forms page is not shown.

Multi-factor prompts, password changes, the page shown after a rejected login, and customized sign-in forms. A sign-in page that is not Outlook Web Access forms-based authentication is not covered at all.

schemaGaps: Case-insensitive path. The adapter compares the lower-cased pathname with /owa/auth/logon.aspx and its test signs in on /OWA/Auth/Logon.aspx. Step paths are compared case-sensitively, so a steps file would refuse servers that answer in another letter case.

Conditions on the form that a step cannot state: no reason query parameter other than 0, a same-origin POST to /owa/auth.owa, exactly one hidden destination field that stays under /owa and outside /owa/auth, and a sign-in control bound to the page's clkLgn() function.
notes: The exchange profile has capability manual and neither a login path nor selectors in the catalog; it becomes automatic only by pointing it at the exchange-owa adapter, which is catalog work outside this directory. That adapter is tested against synthetic forms only: docs/exchange-owa-login.md lines 110-116 say that sign-in on a real server has not been established.
